arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Scott Cooper argued for Austria. He cited the Landgraf case. He claimed Congress did not direct retroactive application of the Act.
Paul Hungar argued for the United States. He stated sovereign immunity bars pre-1976 expropriation claims. He emphasized the consistent position of the U.S. government.
Alan Schoenberg argued for Altmann. He listed four grounds for affirming the lower court. He argued the Act regulates jurisdiction, not primary conduct.
Cooper responded to a question about the Dralle case. He argued that case does not support second-guessing expropriation in Austria.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: Maria Altmann sued Austria in U.S. courts. She sought to recover art her family lost during World War II. Austria argued the Foreign Sovereign Immunities Act does not apply to pre-1976 events. The lower court allowed the lawsuit to proceed. Austria asked the Supreme Court to reverse that decision.

Altmann wants the Supreme Court to affirm the lower court. She seeks to keep her lawsuit alive in U.S. courts.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case determines whether U.S. courts can hear claims about property seized before 1976. It defines the scope of sovereign immunity for foreign states. It impacts how victims of historical seizures seek redress in American courts.
